text:
omar: heads-up — canary pool p99 shot up after the v5 checkpoint onboard at ~08:12. saw ~3x latency on short-chat workloads.

liz: copying perf dashboard. is this when the kernel selector flipped to fallthrough path? :thinking_face:

omar: looks like it. sampler shows kernel_selector chose 'fallback_avx' instead of 'fast_attention' for many requests. probable cause: tokenmap/encoding changed lengths.

jin: any heap/profile traces? I ran perf on one canary pod and saw burst of memcpy + cache misses during kv cache lookup. attaching snippet: 

jin: ```
# perf top (sample)
memcpy               34.2%
kv_cache_lookup       22.8%
fast_attention_kernel 8.9%
fallback_kernel      28.6%
```

aisha: that memcpy spike smells like token remap expansion — new tokenizer emits multi-byte sequences for some emojis, pushing average seq length +2 which trips kernel heuristics.

matt: confirmed with quick stat: average seq len for canary requests jumped from 56 -> 78 after rollout. batch size distribution shifted (more smaller batches).

omar: CI didn't flag this because our unit tests use synthetic uniform lengths. this only surfaced in real traffic.

liz: can we force kernel selector to prefer fast_attention for v5 while we fix tokenmap? i.e., override selector policy per-model?

jin: we do have a per-model kernel_policy flag. devops can set kernel_policy: prefer_fast for the v5 tag. small patch: 

jin: ```json
{"model":"v5","kernel_policy":"prefer_fast"}
```

release-bot: deploy candidate 2026-03-18-08:30 queued to canary.

omar: before we push, we should bisect which change in the onboarding diff caused tokenmap change — tokenizer config drift vs checkpoint token ids. I've started a git bisect between checkpoints: 

omar: ```
git bisect start HEAD v4-checkpoint
# ran token length harness on checkpoints
```

matt: quick note — KV cache stats show increased eviction rate on the canary nodes; cache hit-rate down 7%. likely due to token ids not matching existing cache keys, so warmup cost increased.

aisha: yeah tokenmap mismatch => different keys => cold KV lookups. combined with slower kernel = p99 blowup.

liz: plan suggestions: 1) pause v5 canary rollout, 2) set kernel_policy prefer_fast on canary (short-term), 3) revert tokenmap config in onboarding, 4) add regression test in CI for seq-len distribution. anyone object?

jin: +1 on all. I'll prepare the kernel_policy patch.

matt: I'll run the bisect job and post the exact commit that altered token ids.

omar: infra-bot — pause rollout for model:v5-canary?

infra-bot: ack — pausing rollout for model:v5-canary at 08:44. active connections will drain.

release-bot: patch candidate with kernel_policy applied posted: rc-2890011223-kernel-policy.

jin: pushed the kernel_policy override to canary. monitoring now. initial p99 dropped back to baseline within 2 mins.

omar: great. Next: matt, get the bisect result and PR to revert the offending tokenmap patch. aisha, please own adding a CI harness sampling realistic seq-lengths and tokenmap compatibility checks. liz, can you coordinate a postmortem blameless doc?

liz: on it. will draft summary + action items and add to eng-runtime retro.

matt: bisect found the bad change — commit 6b2f9a7 changed tokenizer fallback encoding for rare unicode sequences. opening revert PR now.

omar: thanks. once revert merges we'll re-run warmup and unpause canary. add a short eval across representative user locales to confirm.

jin: also adding a small selector tweak: add a stability metric that considers kv_cache_hit_rate so we avoid switching to fallback kernels during cache warmup spikes. I'll send a follow-up PR with tests.

aisha: noted. will add token-id compatibility check and a quick perf smoke in pre-merge CI.

liz: closing loop: kernel override + pause = temporary fix, bisect -> revert = root cause, and CI/regression tests = prevention. thanks team :thumbsup:

omar: marking this thread as blocker for next deploy until revert merges.

infra-bot: note — canary paused; alert suppressed.

release-bot: re-run canary once revert merged and KV warmup hits >= 95% on smoke set.

matt: PR 3421 opened to revert 6b2f9a7 and add changelog + test.

omar: awesome. I'll follow up in the postmortem with profiling excerpts and the perf graphs.
